newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish-U.S. Przymierze to launch fund on Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: Polish-U.S. Przymierze to launch fund on Sept 16.

text.p: The Polish-U.S. mutual fund company Przymierze Towarzystwo Funduszy Powierniczych SA will start selling units of its first fund, Eurofundusz 1, on September 16, the company's financial director said on Monday.
Eurofundusz 1 will be a balanced fund of stocks and bonds with a minimum investment of 100 zlotys.
"We start selling units at Bank Pekao SA brokerage outlets on September 16, in exactly two weeks," Slawomir Kolarz told a news conference.
President Tomasz Bankowski said that by the end of next year the company wanted to gain an asset value of about 200 million zlotys, meaning about 50,000 to 60,000 accounts.
Przymierze, which won a Polish operating licence in May, is 51-percent owned by Polish state-owned Bank Pekao SA while the U.S.'s Alliance Capital Management LP has 49 percent.
Bankowski said Przymierze's next fund, most likely an aggressive fund based on stocks, would probably follow no later than in one year, followed by debt instrument funds.
Przymierze has a capital of six million zlotys and is the fourth asset management company cleared to operate an open-ended mutual fund in Poland.
Eurofundusz 1 also has an option for investors to avoid commission charges by investing for at least five years.

Investment director Wojciech Gryko said 103 outlets of Bank Pekao SA brokerage would sell Eurofundusz 1 around Poland, with the firm possibly adding its own outlets and those of four other brokerages over the coming months.
He said the fund would fill up to 10 percent of its portfolio with foreign securities.
